newTerms.Behold the man / Behold your king: Aquí tienen al hombre / Aquí tienen a su rey

forcedChoices.choice: The Jews, the Sanhedrists, and Caiaphas address Pilate with «tú»
forcedChoices.reason: The English shows no great respect here (185:2.4 calls it effrontery), and one form keeps the crowd's shouts «¡Crucifícalo!» consistent.
A wife writes to her husband.
The English «he» can be Pilate or the false Messiah; Spanish keeps the subject implicit, so both readings stay open.
Two questions joined by a comma keep one sentence, as the English dash does.
